note.explanation: Binomial nomenclature is the system of giving each organism a two-part scientific name. The first part names its genus and the second part names its species. This standard name is used worldwide, helping biologists communicate clearly even when they speak different languages.
note.checkAnswer: The genus name comes first and begins with a capital letter; the species name comes second and begins with a small letter.
note.simple: Each organism gets a two-word scientific name: first its genus, then its species.
note.checkQuestion: In *Panthera tigris*, which word is the genus name?
note.title: Binomial Nomenclature
steps: Write the genus name first, beginning with a capital letter.
Write the species name second, beginning with a small letter.
Use italics when printing the scientific name.
If handwriting the name, underline its two parts separately.
note.answer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of scientific naming in which each organism's name has two parts: its genus name followed by its species name.

written.text: How does binomial nomenclature facilitate clear communication about organisms across different languages?
written.finalAnswer: Binomial nomenclature gives each organism a unique scientific name that is the same anywhere in the world. The names are taken from Latin, so no country is favoured. Biologists can use this standard name to communicate clearly, whatever language they speak.

written.text: Imagine you discover a new organism. What steps would you take to classify and name it according to the principles of binomial nomenclature?
written.finalAnswer: I would study the organism's characteristics and compare them with known organisms to decide its classification. I would print the name in italics or, when handwriting it, underline the two parts separately.

explain.title: What binomial nomenclature means
explain.body: The system of scientific naming of organisms is termed as binomial nomenclature. The scientific name has two parts: the genus name first and the species name second.

explain.title: Why scientific names are useful
explain.body: Common names can change between regions, and one common name may be used for several organisms. Scientific names give biologists a unique, standard name to use worldwide, whatever language they speak.

explain.title: Rules for writing a scientific name
explain.body: Scientific names use words from Latin and should be unique. Write the genus first with a capital letter and the species second with a small letter. Use italics in print; when writing by hand, underline the two parts separately.

mistakes: Putting the species name before the genus name.

Writing the genus name with a small initial letter.

Underlining both parts together instead of separately when handwriting the name.
Treating a common name as a scientific name or assuming common names are the same everywhere.
